title: P2 — revisionLag metric can never report real lag once local row versions are corrupted (and is fragile by design): buildLocalStatusPayload computes maxVersion = computeWatermark(local tables) and revisionLag = max(0, maxVersion - lastAppliedRevision). Even without FED-020, lag should be measured against CENTRAL's advertised watermark (the delta payload's maxVersion), not the edge's own rows. FIX: track central's last-advertised maxVersion (edge already receives it in every snapshot/delta payload) and compute revisionLag from that; add a regression test: edge at rev N, central at N+2 → local-status revisionLag == 2 (not 0). PASS: after FED-020 fix, a stale edge (simulate by pausing sync) reports revisionLag > 0.

title: [foreman-found t379] tests/unit/xai-oauth-service.test.js is load-fragile: positional fetch-mock queue misaligns under machine load, producing false-red Tier-1 guard and Tier-2 judge verdicts
detail: Foreman-found at tick 379 while screening the pending set. Under the fleet's normal machine load (uptime loadavg 10-25) this 125-line unit file intermittently fails with (a) 'Test timed out in 5000ms' and (b) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ok') at src/lib/oauth/providers/xai.js:74. Mechanism: every test resets the global fetch stub in beforeEach and then queues canned responses positionally with fetch.mockResolvedValueOnce(...), so the meaning of each queued response depends on CALL ORDER; an extra or out-of-order fetch consumes a queued slot and a later call resolves undefined. The assertions compound the fragility by indexing fetch.mock.calls[1]. The file passes 5/5 in isolation in ~1.6s (measured this tick at loadavg 10.74), so no product code is at fault. Cost of the defect: the repo's pre-commit hook (GitReins Tier-1) runs the full vitest suite, so a load spike turns a clean tree into a BLOCKED commit and a judge run into tier1 FAIL / 'REGRESSION: 2 test pass->fail'; documented across ticks 143/192/372 and again at tick 378, where the board-chore commit was blocked by the hook and only passed on retry. FIX DIRECTION (dispatched this tick): dispatch the fetch response by URL via mockImplementation instead of position, locate assertions by URL instead of call index, and give the file an explicit 30s testTimeout so load-induced latency cannot trip the 5s default. The replica/delta story compounds it: a deleted key still validates on an edge that replicated the tombstone. title: [foreman-t401] State-DB corruption has no proven path: a malformed DATA_DIR/db/data.sqlite kills startup with a MISLEADING 'No SQLite driver available' error, and an emptied file is silently reset to an empty DB — no detection, no preservation, no backup restore, no operator-visible message
detail:
Foreman repro 2026-09-19 (node 22.22.3, driver chain better-sqlite3 -> node:sqlite -> sql.js, isolated DATA_DIR=/tmp/9r-dbprobe, direct src/lib/db/driver.js import):
(1) TRUNCATED file: seed a DB via getAdapter() (migrations #1..#5, row probe_marker='SURVIVES'); then `truncate -s 1024 db/data.sqlite` (WAL deleted AND with WAL kept, both measured) and re-open in a fresh process -> all four adapters report `database disk image is malformed` and driver.js:68 throws `Error: [DB] No SQLite driver available (bun/better/node/sql.js all failed)`. The message blames missing drivers, not the corrupt file; the path is not named; the corrupt bytes are left in place; DATA_DIR/db/backups is never consulted; nothing is preserved.
(2) GARBAGE file: 512 random bytes at the same path -> identical misleading fatal.
(3) EMPTY file: `: > db/data.sqlite` -> treated as a FRESH install: migrations #1..#5 re-applied, first read of the previous schema throws `no such table: probe_marker`, exit 0, NO warning at all -> total silent data loss (every provider connection, API key and setting).
(4) Source: `grep -rn -iE 'SQLITE_CORRUPT|corrupt|malformed' src/lib/db/ src/lib/dataDir.mjs` = ZERO hits — there is no corruption handling in the DB layer. src/lib/db/backup.js documents in its own header: 'Backups are a best-effort safety net before schema migrations. There is NO automated restore path; recovery is manual (copy a backup file back).' Backups are written ONLY before a schema change (makeBackupDir/backupDbLite via migrate.js), KEEP_BACKUPS=3.
Origin rows: QA-9ROUTER-11 (P2, still pending) whose chaos-corruption cell truncated the gitignored .vfs/graph/graph.db — a rebuildable fleet cache, not app state — and scored INFO with next-start behavior UNVERIFIED; QA-9ROUTER-22 first-hand observed the silent-reset shape on 2026-09-18 and answered that the real state DB is DATA_DIR/db/data.sqlite. This row is the repo-owned half: make the real state DB's corruption behavior detected, preserved, recoverable and asserted.
FIX SHAPE: (a) detect a malformed/headerless DATA_FILE before the adapter chain swallows it (SQLite header magic + PRAGMA quick_check on a probe connection, and/or classify the adapters' 'malformed' error separately from module-load failures); (b) preserve the corrupt file as data.sqlite.corrupt-<ts> (never overwrite in place); (c) restore the newest usable entry under DATA_DIR/db/backups when one exists, with a loud message, else start empty but LOUDLY (never silently); (d) never let the operator see 'No SQLite driver available' when the real cause is a malformed DB file — a genuinely missing module must keep the existing per-adapter 'unavailable' warnings.
PASS: (1) malformed and empty-file cases each produce a distinct, actionable error naming the path and the true cause, with the original bytes preserved under a .corrupt-* name; (2) with a valid backup present the restored data is readable (assert the seeded row's CONTENT, not merely 'no throw'); (3) healthy-DB negative control: no rename, no warning, rows intact; (4) a deterministic vitest under tests/ (temp DATA_DIR, no network, module-registry reset) that the foreman proves LOAD-BEARING by removing the detection and watching it go red; (5) `node tests/__baseline__/verify-no-regression.mjs` shows no new pass->fail vs the current known-fails baseline and `npm run lint:gate` shows no NEW/INCREASED problem; (6) CHANGELOG.md records the user-visible behavior change.

Battery docker-deploy cell graded INFO 'compose up OK, no HTTP response within 60s (probe deadline exhausted)' - that is a lie of omission: the container never served because it crashed at boot. Per-cell evidence, harvested from the live agent BEFORE collect: (a) dc.log tail - the only reason compose up returned OK is `pnpm/docker compose` printing success while the container dies child-first; (b) ep.log (chaos-errorpath) - `Error: Cannot find module /home/bunker-652fa075/qa-noconfig-2706562/custom-server.js` (MODULE_NOT_FOUND, node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1433); (c) ui.log - the dev-mode leg boots Next.js 16.3.6 and dies at `[DB][migrate] applied #5 federation-central-watermark` then `* Compiling /login ...`. Dev-box reproduction of the same class at HEAD 04f4a7bc: `PORT=25128 docker compose -p qa9router -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local-build.yml up -d --build --no-deps 9router` -> build OK, container started, first probe `/api/health` answered 200 (dev box has node_modules/ present via the build context), then the container was gone. Static drift root cause, independent of the run: Dockerfile runner stage copies `src/lib/federation`, `src/lib/db`, `src/lib/dataDir.mjs` and `src/mitm` only (grep the COPY lines), but the documented runtime entrypoint custom-server.js resolves `@/lib/...` for the general runtime surface (logger, settings, keys) - `src/lib/dataDir.mjs` exists in the runner image while its siblings (e.g. src/lib/logger.js, which exists in the repo at HEAD) do not. Second, the compose coexistence defect already closed as DF-9ROUTER-48 (complete) is NOT fixed at HEAD: `docker-compose.yml` still pins `volumes: 9router-data: name: 9router-data`; verbatim probe at this HEAD: `PORT=25129 docker compose -p qa9router2 -f docker-compose.yml config --format json` resolves volumes {'9router-data': {'name': '9router-data'}} - a GLOBAL volume name, and the teardown line in the run log `Volume 9router-data Removing` shows why one of these probes removed state from outside its project. Remedy: copy the full runtime surface the entrypoint needs (or let Next standalone tracing emit it), and drop the explicit volume name.

title: [P1] Docker build fails deterministically at the export stage on unchanged inputs: RUN mkdir -p /app/data && chown -R node:node /app times out (140.2s) over a 16.5GB build context
reasoning: QA foreman cycle 2026-09-29 - fresh-system CI pass on bunker-mvp (docker-deploy leg) + off-battery docker-build stage
detail: Reproduced on the dev box at HEAD 04f4a7bc with the documented clean-host command `PORT=25128 docker compose -p qa9router -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local-build.yml up -d --build --no-deps 9router`: the build reads the checkout as its context (`[9router internal] load build context / transferring context: 1.14GB 3.0s done` is the FILTERED byte count after .dockerignore) and every prior step succeeds (next build --webpack completes, 147 static pages generated), then the final runner step `RUN mkdir -p /app/data && chown -R node:node /app && mkdir -p /app/data-home && chown node:node /app/data-home && ln -sf /app/data-home /root/.9router` reports `DONE 140.2s` and the `exporting to image` / `exporting layers` stage never finishes: rc from the whole compose up was non-zero and the exported image `9router:local` was never a servable reference (subsequent `docker inspect` on the compose-suffixed container name returned 'No such container'). The same step is the only one that walks the entire copied tree: with node_modules shipped in the context (the local-build path COPY . ./ after npm ci) that chown touches hundreds of thousands of files. Fix direction: chown only the paths that need it (/app/data, /app/data-home, the .next/standalone subtree) instead of `-R /app`, and/or exclude node_modules from the local-build context via .dockerignore.
